item.title: 20 Questions With Doc Martin: What the ’90s L.A. Rave Scene Was Really Like & Remembering His Friend DJ Dan
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the world of music and explore the stories behind the artists. Today, we're talking about a legend in the West Coast dance music scene, Doc Martin. Born Martin Mendoza in San Francisco, Doc Martin has been spinning tracks for over three decades, helping define the early '90s rave scene in Los Angeles.
[Music transitions to a West Coast dance music track]
Host: Doc Martin started his career spinning on vinyl, and was a key figure in the Los Angeles rave scene, alongside artists like DJ Dan and Marques Wyatt. He's also the founder of the Sublevel label, which has been running strong for 30 years.
[Music transitions to an interview clip with Doc Martin]
Doc Martin: I'm in Oceanside, California, and it's 70 degrees year round, and by the beach — less than two miles away from the water.
Host: Doc Martin is getting ready for a summer tour, with stops at the Om Records Retreat, Flash in Washington D.C., and the Shambhala festival in British Columbia. We caught up with him to talk about his career, his music, and what's next.
[Music transitions to an interview clip with Doc Martin]
Doc Martin: My mom was a hairdresser for Vidal Sassoon and Paul Mitchell, she taught at his school and also sang backups for a couple of local bands like Paul Revere & The Raiders in San Francisco. My dad was an upholsterer... my mom, up until five years ago, was still in that mode of "When are you going to get a real job?" Now she kind of sees the light, finally, after 35 years.
Host: Doc Martin's passion for music is still going strong, and he's got some exciting shows coming up. If you're new to electronic music, he recommends checking out the first Future Sound Of London record, Accelerator.
[Music transitions to an electronic music track]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. If you want to learn more about Doc Martin and his upcoming shows, check out our website for more information. Until next time, keep dancing!
[Outro music plays]
